subject.title: Carson — Measure CU (City Government Accountability, Charter Update, No Tax Increase)

strong: Carson City Government Accountability, Charter Update, No Tax Increase Measure.

text: Shall the measure amending the Carson City Charter to require campaign contribution transparency; make the City Charter consistent with State law on referring ballot measures for voter approval; update term limits to increase voter options; update City Treasurer duties; clarify and clean up inconsistent or outdated language, be adopted?
Lula Davis-Holmes, Mayor; Cedric Hicks, Mayor Pro Tem; Jawane Hilton, Councilmember; Arleen Rojas, Councilmember; Darrow's New Orleans Grill
None submitted.

fullText.title: Full Text of Ballot Measure Cu

strong: CHARTER SECTIONS TO BE AMENDED (ADDITIONS SHOWN IN BOLD AND DELETIONS IN ):
Note: Portions of the listed sections which are not shown below are not amended.

text: The elective officers of the City shall consist of four city council members, one directly elected mayor, a city clerk, and a city treasurer,

strong: either through at large or district elections, as determined by the city council. For any district elections,

text: the members of the city council shall be elected by the voters from

strong: and the mayor shall be elected by a citywide vote

text: at the time and in the manner provided in this Charter.

strong: For any at large elections, city council members and the mayor will be elected by a citywide vote.

text: In the event that the population of the City exceeds one hundred thousand (100,000) residents, by resolution of the city council, the City may increase the elective officers of the City to six city council members, one directly elected mayor, a city clerk, and a city treasurer.

All elective officers shall serve for a term of four years and until their respective successors are elected and qualified. The elective officers in office at the time this Charter takes effect shall continue in office until the termination of their current terms and succeeding terms shall be likewise for four (4) years.

strong: There shall be no limit on the number of terms that elective officers may serve.

text: The term of each elective officer shall commence no later than five days from the certification of the election results by the city council. Ties in voting among candidates for officer shall be settled by lot.
Elective officers and employees shall have the same indemnification rights as specified under California State law only.

B. Filling Vacancy. A vacancy on the city council, from whatever cause, may be filled by appointment by a majority of the remaining members of the city council, or by the calling of a special election if no appointment is made within sixty (60) days of the commencement of the vacancy. No person shall be eligible to fill a vacancy unless, at the time of appointment, they are a qualified elector of the City

have been domiciled in the City for at least sixty (60) days immediately preceding his or her appointment. Any person appointed or elected to fill a vacancy on the city council shall serve the remaining unexpired term of the office. In the event it shall fail to fill a vacancy by appointment within sixty (60) days after such office shall become vacant, the city council shall cause an election to fill such vacancy to be held at the next available state election, but not less than 114 days from the call of the special election. The times and procedures for the calling of any special election to fill a city council vacancy may be established by City ordinance consistent with State law.
B. City Manager Authority to Contract. By ordinance or resolution the city council may authorize the city manager

strong: to approve any contract for any subject matter so long as such approval complies with applicable law. By ordinance or resolution the city council may also authorize the city manager

text: to bind the City, with a written contract, including by purchase order, for the acquisition of equipment, materials, supplies, labor, services or other items included within the budget approved by the city council, and shall by ordinance impose a monetary limit upon such authority as authorized by this Charter.
D. Sale of Real Property. No real property of City
be sold, transferred or conveyed
without city council

. Moreover, real property valued at more than two million five hundred thousand dollars ($2,500,000), may not be sold, transferred or conveyed except when approved by ordinance or resolution passed by a two-thirds affirmative vote of the city council.
E. Acquisition of Real Property. Any real property which is sold, dedicated, or transferred to City
must be accepted by resolution of the city council.
(1) General Tax. The city council shall not impose, extend, or increase any general tax for general government purposes unless and until that tax is submitted to the electorate

vote of the city council and approved by a majority vote of the voters. A general tax shall not be deemed to have been increased if it is imposed at a rate not higher than the maximum rate so approved.
(2) Special Tax. The city council shall not impose, extend, or increase any special tax for specific purposes unless and until that tax is submitted to the electorate

vote of the city council and approved by a two-thirds vote of the voters. A special tax shall not be deemed to have been increased if it is imposed at a rate not higher than the maximum rate so approved.

Each City councilmember and mayor must comply with state disclosure laws for campaign donations. The City's local donation disclosure rules shall not be less stringent than those of the state; City may not increase the minimum donation reporting threshold to be higher than the dollar threshold required under state law.
The City shall remove all references to a fixed year date contained in the provisions of the charter and Sections 305, 502 (8), 502 (9), and 907 (4) shall be deleted in their entirety.

analysis.title: City Attorney's Impartial Analysis of Measure Cu

text: Measure CU was placed on the ballot by the Carson City Council and proposes amendments to specified provisions of the Carson City Charter. If adopted, Measure CU would amend the Charter as follows:
Measure CU would amend Section 301 to provide that City Councilmembers may be elected either at large or by district, as determined by the City Council.

Measure CU would add Section 320 incorporating State campaign-contribution disclosure requirements applicable to the Mayor and City Councilmembers into the Charter and provide that local disclosure requirements may not be less stringent than State law.
Section 907(1)&(2) currently require a two-thirds Council vote to submit a tax to voters. Measure CU would change that to require a majority affirmative vote for submission of a tax to the voters.

Measure CU would repeal Section 907(4), which places Charter-specific restrictions on additional taxes and certain environmental requirements applicable to oil refineries and petroleum-product storage facilities subject to the City’s Oil Industry Business License Tax. Repeal would remove those restrictions, but would not itself impose or increase any tax.

The measure would repeal Section 305, which limits City Councilmembers to three four-year terms and clarifies all elective officers are not subject to term limits, and amend Section 301 to make it consistent with repeal of Section 305. This change clarifies that going forward all elective officers are not subject to term limits. Section 306 would also be amended to remove the related term-limit restriction on appointments to fill City Council vacancies.

The Charter permits the City Council to delegate specified contracting authority to the City Manager for budgeted acquisitions, subject to a monetary limit. Section 319 would permit the Council, by ordinance or resolution, to authorize the City Manager to approve contracts on any subject matter, subject to applicable state law.

Section 319 would also be amended regarding City real property. For property the City sells, transfers, or conveys in fee, the measure would eliminate the requirement for a Planning Commission finding regarding General Plan consistency and instead require City Council approval by resolution. The existing two-thirds Council-vote requirement for property valued above $2.5 million would remain. For property acquired by the City, Council acceptance by resolution would apply only to property acquired in fee.

Measure CU would delete Sections 502(8) and 502(9), removing Charter provisions assigning the City Treasurer specified investment-policy duties and requiring the Treasurer to chair an investment committee. The Treasurer’s other Charter duties would remain.
The measure would also remove fixed-year references and make conforming and cleanup changes.

A “YES” vote on Measure CU is a vote in favor of the proposed Charter amendments. A “NO” vote on Measure CU is a vote against the proposed Charter amendments. Measure CU takes effect if approved by a majority of those voting on the measure and after acceptance and filing by the California Secretary of State.

SUNNY SOLTANI
City Attorney, City of Carson
